title: Folder sync engine with a shared batch runner
name: File sync engine

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies a sync plan, including the repeated-looking batch calls in Apply? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The three runBatch calls in Apply are structurally alike. What does extracting runBatch buy here, compared with three hand-written loops?
choices: Concurrency limits, cancellation handling and error aggregation are fixed in one place, so a fix or policy change applies to uploads, downloads and deletes at once
It makes uploads, downloads and deletes run in parallel with each other
It guarantees that all changes are applied atomically or not at all
It removes the need for Plan because the items are generic

questions.prompt: One download in a batch returns an error. What happens to the other items?
choices: The errgroup context is cancelled and all in-flight transfers abort
Remaining items are skipped and only the first error is returned
The failure is recorded for that index, the other items still run, and every failure is returned in one joined error
The batch retries the failed item until it succeeds

questions.prompt: In download, the checksum is verified before os.Rename. Why is the file written to a temp file in the destination directory first?
choices: os.Rename only works for files in the system temp directory

A concurrent reader of the path never sees a partially written or corrupted file: the destination is replaced atomically only after the content is verified, and a same-directory temp avoids a cross-filesystem rename
It lets the engine resume partial downloads later
It avoids calling Close on the body
